title: Error fetching file in Cursor
author: KiraEzy

comments.body: Please use the bug request template when opening an issue and include the details requested in there. This issue happened more frequently on older versions of the MCP server, mostly related to people having network-level proxy servers.

Please when you write an answer to an issue you already know happened before, provide 1 or 2 solution steps or reference to the previous threads so that we can see the solutions. Best is when you use the answer request template for answering people in github issues. If you do not have one, ask your boss.

> I typed in the access token, start the server through npx, then asked in Agent mode and it called MCP tool with get_figma_data, but with result: Error fetching file: [object Object], in the console hosting the npx, Error fetching file xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx: { status: 403, err: 'Forbidden' } is shown

The reason why it was not working for me was related to Figma and the project itself. It was in a draft. It should be in your projects. Additionally, I did copy the whole project to my projects so that I am the owner. 

But I also made sure the correct structure: 

```
"mcpServers": {
  "Framelink Figma MCP": {
    "command": "npx",
    "args": [
      "-y",
      "figma-developer-mcp",
      "--figma-api-key=YOUR_ACCESS_TOKEN",
      "--stdio"
    ]
  }
}
```

 🧪 Optional Debug Tip:
To debug, you can run this manually in your terminal to test if the MCP works:

`npx -y figma-developer-mcp --figma-api-key=YOUR_ACCESS_TOKEN --stdio`

If it works, you should see it wait for input (it’s ready to receive messages from Cursor).


✅ So what's next if the above command works?

If you’re still seeing errors like “403 Forbidden”, then the issue is not your MCP setup, but most likely one of the following:

1. Access Permissions
        Make sure the Figma file you’re accessing is:
        
        Owned by the same account tied to your access token
        
        Or shared with your account
        
        If it’s in a team or org, make sure your API token has access to that team/file
        
2. Incorrect node ID
        Make sure the node ID is valid and exists in the Figma file.
        
        You can open the Figma file, select the element, and copy the node ID from the URL or dev tools.

3. File is not accessible via API
        The file might be private or not shared properly with the token's user.
        
        Open the file in Figma, go to Share, and ensure the user linked to the access token has at least view access.

title: [Request/Question] Filter out hidden nodes
body:
Thank you for this amazing Figma MCP server! It's been incredibly helpful for my design workflow with Cursor.

## Feature Idea

I was wondering if it might be possible to add an option to filter out nodes where `visible === false` from the response data?

## Why I'm suggesting this

I've noticed that when working with component-heavy Figma files, there are often many hidden nodes that don't contribute to the actual design but still get included in the context. These hidden elements:

- Make the context unnecessarily large
- Can sometimes confuse the AI model
- Might reduce the accuracy of the generated code

I did a quick experiment by manually filtering these nodes in Cursor and was pleasantly surprised by the improvement in both response quality and implementation accuracy!
author: StereoApp

comments.body: Great idea—this is coming soon thanks to @Li-vien!
This is completed as of #13

title: feat: Extracting global variables
body:
## changelog
1.  Extract all attribute objects to globalVars to reduce the volume of simplifiedResponse and facilitate AI to extract variables
2.  Extract vector elements that are not easy to implement in code and convert them into image nodes.
3.  Ignore all hidden nodes and empty nodes
4.  Add a new get_image tools to download the image of the vector node. You can tell AI to "download the image node to local" to trigger it.
author: Li-vien

comments.body: I am excited to take this for a spin. Thanks for putting it together! Will report back shortly 🫡

This is an awesome upgrade. I wouldn't have guessed that AI could follow the style references when they're so far away in the JSON, but it's really quite good at it.

In my testing it looks like this change further reduces the metadata payload ~40–50%. Compared to the raw response from Figma our data is about 20% the size.

So good—thank you for the contribution!

body:

The MCP server is running locally and properly configured in Cursor (the green light is on and I can see the logs from the server saying the connection was made). I've also tested it with the `pnpm inspect` command and am able to receive API responses for both `get-file` and `get-node`.

Am I missing something in terms Cursor config?

Thank you
author: nicholasc

comments.body:
There was a bug with Cursor that made the kebab-case function names unreliable. Can you pull a new version of the server and try again? The newest version uses snake_case and should be more reliable. Cursor is also working on a stability improvement on their end that should address it there as well.

If the newest version of the MCP server has issues for you let me know and we can look more closely.

Following up, you should be able to run `npx figma-developer-mcp --figma-api-key=<your_key>` and get the latest version without needing to pull code or run it in dev mode. Give that a shot and see if it works better if the above doesn't work.
Closing this issue for now—reopen if there are still issues you're running into @nicholasc!
